input.hypothesis: The US extends semiconductor export controls to legacy nodes

nodes.statement: BIS publishes a rule extending US semiconductor export controls to legacy-node (≥28nm) chips or equipment by 2026-06-30
nodes.resolution: Federal Register notice from BIS covering mature-node chips/tools; resolves YES on publication, NO if 180 days pass without one
nodes.rationale: BIS has signaled mature-node scrutiny (2024 RFI, Section 232 semiconductor probe). Reference class: prior control expansions (Oct 2022, Oct 2023, Dec 2024 HBM rule) took 6-18 months from signal to rule. A legacy rule is contested internally, so base rate below 50%.
assumptions: BIS retains rulemaking staff capacity through 2026
No US-China détente freezes new controls
nodes.marketQuery: Will BIS extend semiconductor export controls to legacy-node chips before 2026-06-30?

nodes.statement: Commerce Section 232 semiconductor investigation concludes national-security threat finding citing mature-node capacity
nodes.resolution: Public 232 report or presidential action citing legacy chips; resolves on official release
nodes.rationale: 232 probe initiated Sep 2025; statutory timeline and precedent (steel/aluminum) favor an affirmative finding. It is the cleanest legal vehicle for legacy-node controls.
assumptions: Report is not withheld for negotiation leverage
Findings cover chips, not only downstream products
nodes.marketQuery: Will the Section 232 semiconductor investigation produce an affirmative national security finding by 2026-06-30?

nodes.statement: China retaliates against US chipmakers or toolmakers (entity-list additions, procurement bans) within 60 days of any legacy rule
nodes.resolution: MOFCOM announcement or official Chinese measures targeting US semiconductor firms after a legacy rule
nodes.rationale: Analog: China's Apr 2025 rare-earth and entity responses followed US controls within weeks. Legacy-node controls hit Chinese industrial champions directly, raising retaliation odds versus prior rules.
assumptions: Retaliation targets US firms, not only symbolic goods
China does not pre-empt with talks
nodes.marketQuery: Will China announce semiconductor-related retaliation against US firms within 60 days of new US legacy-node controls?

nodes.statement: Final legacy rule is narrower than proposed (equipment-only or China-only, no broad chip licensing)
nodes.resolution: Published rule scope excludes broad legacy-chip licensing; resolves on rule text
nodes.rationale: Inhibitor path: broad legacy controls would raise US consumer/industrial costs; industry lobbying (autos, power) historically narrows scope, as in the 2024 Section 301 tariff carve-outs.
assumptions: Domestic cost pressure outweighs hawkish pressure
Lobbying window exists before final rule
nodes.marketQuery: Will the final US legacy-node export rule be limited to equipment or China-only scope?

nodes.statement: SMH falls more than 10% from announcement-date level within 30 days of a broad legacy rule
nodes.resolution: Close-to-close drawdown >10% from the close on rule-publication day, within 30 calendar days
nodes.rationale: Analog: SMH dropped ~8-12% in the month after Oct 2022 controls; a legacy rule hits a larger revenue base (mature-node equipment, fabs), but index is now more AI-weighted, damping beta.
assumptions: No offsetting AI earnings surprise in window
nodes.marketQuery: Will SMH decline more than 10% within 30 days of new legacy-node export controls?

nodes.name: VanEck Semiconductor ETF
nodes.rationale: Legacy controls pressure equipment and China-exposed names; AI-heavy weights and possible narrow rule cap downside. Baseline modest decline with wide sigma reflecting rule-scope uncertainty.

nodes.name: Applied Materials
nodes.rationale: Mature-node deposition/etch tools are a large China revenue share; direct target of any equipment-side legacy rule. Analog: AMAT fell ~15% on Oct 2022 rule over a month.
assumptions: Rule covers tools, not chips only

nodes.name: Texas Instruments
nodes.rationale: Counter-force: TXN is a US legacy-node producer; controls on Chinese mature-node supply raise its pricing power and US share, partially offsetting sector weakness.
assumptions: Rule restricts Chinese legacy chips into US
No Chinese retaliation on TXN products

nodes.name: SOX Philadelphia Semiconductor Index
nodes.rationale: Sector-level proxy; historical control-event drawdowns of 3-12% with 20-40 day lags inform baseline and sigma.

edges.mechanism: Affirmative 232 finding supplies legal predicate and political cover for BIS legacy-node rulemaking
assumptions: BIS acts within 90 days of finding

edges.mechanism: Chinese retaliation playbook against US semiconductor firms after each control round
Industry and downstream-user lobbying narrows final rule scope
Control announcements trigger sector de-rating on China revenue risk
Narrow rule removes the drawdown catalyst
Retaliation deepens China revenue uncertainty for US chip/toolmakers
Sector beta to control events; AI weights damp legacy exposure
Direct equipment-control exposure via China mature-node tool sales
Counter-force: US legacy producer gains pricing power from restricted Chinese supply
assumptions: Rule restricts Chinese chips into US

edges.mechanism: Index-level sensitivity to export-control shocks per historical analogs

summary.headline: Legacy-node export controls by mid-2026 are a ~22% event, most likely via a Section 232 predicate; a broad rule would hit equipment makers (AMAT) hardest while US legacy producers (TXN) could benefit, and rule-narrowing is the key inhibitor.
summary.mainUncertainty: Whether the final rule is broad (chips + equipment, China-wide) or narrowed to equipment-only scope — this swings both probability of passage and market impact.
followUps: Track Section 232 semiconductor report release and its mature-node language
Monitor BIS pre-publication rule drafts and OIRA review for scope signals
Watch Chinese MOFCOM/entity-list responses within 60 days of any rule
Check SMH/AMAT China revenue disclosures in upcoming earnings
